body:
Add jenga-push-and-stack: play one turn of Jenga by the printed Hasbro rules.

A freshly built Jenga Classic tower (54 blocks, 18 levels) stands on the table. The robot must take a block from below the top level, using one hand at a time, and stack it on top crosswise to the top level, with the tower still standing 5 s later. Block thicknesses vary per seed (+-0.3 mm), so some blocks are pinched by the load above and others are loose; nothing visible tells them apart.

Instruction: "Play one turn of Jenga: using one hand at a time, take a block out from below the top level and stack it on top, crosswise to the top level, without knocking the tower over."

Category: Societal relatability.

Scoring: 0 if the tower falls or both grippers touch the tower at once. Otherwise, for the taken block: 1.0 stacked crosswise on top, released, still 5 s later; 0.6 out of the tower; 0.3 slid out half its length; 0.1 slid 5 mm. Capped at 0.1 if any other block ever moved 1 cm, or is 5 mm out of place at the end.

Run limit: 3,000 steps (150 s at 20 Hz).

Scores: Dream-1 run 0.0; scripted demo 1.0 on seeds 0, 4 and 10.
